lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the spring, when kings go out to battle, David stayed in Jerusalem and walked on his roof. From there he saw a woman bathing, and he sent to learn who she was.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She was Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah the Hittite, one of David's own mighty men. David took her, and the child she carried was his.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: Send for Uriah. Let him come to me and sleep in his own house. Then we will know whether the child is his.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Uriah came. He would not eat or sleep in his own house while his comrades fought under the walls of Rabbah. The king's plan would not work.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: Put Uriah at the front of the fight. Let the fiercest men surround him. Then retreat and leave him exposed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Uriah fell and was killed. The messenger ran to David with the news, and the king said nothing at all. The city kept its silence.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The child born to Bathsheba fell ill and died within days. David held the infant and wept, but he could not undo what had been done.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: The most dangerous thing a king can do is use his power to make a wrong thing look like a right one. The roof was only a roof until he looked from it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The king had taken what was not his to take and killed the man who would not help him hide it. The story does not end with a good choice.

choices.label: Wait for the prophet's word 📜
choices.note: Truth spoken by another is the only road back from here.

choices.label: Build the palace higher and forget 🏗️
choices.note: A greater roof might hide the old one from sight.
